extracted.intended_audience: EPO IPEA examiners; patent applicants and agents handling PCT Chapter II (international preliminary examination) procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and evaluative criteria for conducting international preliminary examination (Chapter II PCT) at the EPO acting as IPEA, and for interactions with applicants (telephone consultations, top-up searches, unity protests, time limits, IPER content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of SISR when establishing the IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPER has not yet been established, the examiner will take the SISR into account when establishing the IPER; the examiner waits until 27 months from the priority date to establish the IPER to allow the SISR to arrive and be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a WO-IPEA needs to be sent out before the IPER is established, the examiner waits until 27 months from the priority date to establish the IPER so the SISR can be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for applicant when demand is received very late
rubrics_metrics.description: If the demand has been validly received by the EPO very late, the examiner will telephone the applicant and explain the situation and ask whether the applicant prefers one of several options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant choices include: (i) discuss the application over the phone and receive a short time limit to file amendments (e.g. one to two weeks); (ii) receive a WO-IPEA with a short time limit (e.g. one to two weeks); (iii) receive a negative IPER without further interaction; (iv) receive a WO-IPEA with a longer time limit, in which case the IPER will be issued late. If even a short extension would cause IPER after 28 months, applicant is asked whether they still want a time limit or prefer a timely negative IPER. In exceptional cases where applicant declines amendments and agrees to a negative IPER, examiner sends a direct negative IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting a request for a further written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant explicitly asks for a further written opinion under Chapter II and the examiner's opinion is still negative, the request must be granted if the applicant has not yet had a further opportunity to file amendments in Chapter II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant has already had a further opportunity to file amendments, then as a rule the IPER is issued directly (see GL/PCT-EPO C-IV, 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of late-filed replies relative to IPER timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A late reply to a written opinion may or may not be taken into account depending on whether it is received before the IPER has been started and depending on whether it meets outstanding objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If received after the WO-IPEA time limit but before IPER started, the reply is taken into consideration for drawing up the IPER. If received after IPER has been started and not all objections set out in the last WO-IPEA have been met, the late reply is not considered. If received after IPER started and all objections have been met, the late reply is taken into account. If no reply received, IPER is drawn up on basis of last WO-IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: only searched subject-matter is examinable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search covered only some claims or part of claims, only the subject-matter which has been searched (as indicated in the ISR and/or WO-ISA) can be the object of the international preliminary examination; it should always be made clear which claims have been examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amended claims introducing unsearched matter will not be given an opinion in the IPER (indicate this under Section III with reasons on separate sheet). The IPEA has no responsibility for actions taken by the ISA and there is no PCT provision for an IPEA review/appeal of such ISA decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant arguments about completeness of search not treated as IPEA communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Written arguments from the applicant relating to completeness of the search are not to be treated as a communication with the IPEA, unless the reply contains a complaint against findings at the search stage when the EPO acted as ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply challenges ISA findings related to restriction of the search, the examiner will mention in the WO-IPEA or IPER (under Section III) that the ISA's findings cannot be reviewed by the IPEA. If applicant phones, examiner informs applicant that search completeness is the ISA's responsibility and that Chapter I procedure is closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences in later European procedure when search was restricted or absent
rubrics_metrics.description: For unsearched subject-matter no written opinion under PCT Chapter I and no Chapter II examination is carried out; however, in the European phase the examining division must review the search division's decision and may perform a complete search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the applicant convinces the IPEA under Chapter II that a decision not to search certain subject-matter was incorrect, this has no PCT consequence; in the European phase, the examiner might reverse the ISA decision and perform a complete search (see GL/EPO C-IV, 7.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up search mandatory at outset of Chapter II (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A top-up search is mandatory at the outset of PCT Chapter II, subject to specified exceptions; the date or absence of this top-up search must be indicated in the IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-up search usually conducted before/at same time as issuing the first WO-IPEA/telephone consultation or, where no written opinion is produced, the IPER (approx. 23 months from priority date). The IPER must indicate whether a top-up search has been done and the date of the latest top-up search. The 'no top-up search' box is ticked only if all claims are exempted from top-up search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and basis of top-up search in non-unity cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In non-unity cases with more than one invention claimed for which Chapter II examination is demanded, the examiner will first issue an invitation to pay additional examination fees (Form 405) and then perform the top-up search for those inventions for which additional examination fees have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A further top-up search before issuance of the IPER is normally not necessary. Rules and GL references apply (Rules 66.1ter, 70.2(f), GL/ISPE citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from top-up search
rubrics_metrics.description: A top-up search is not conducted on certain categories of subject-matter or in specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions include: (a) subject-matter not searched by the ISA; (b) non-unity cases—inventions for which additional search fees were paid but not additional examination fees; (c) subject-matter excluded from preliminary examination; (d) where amendments contain added matter (top-up search may be refused or limited, but examiner will perform top-up based on previous or amended documents ignoring added matter); (e) where no letter explains basis for amendments and/or indicates what has been amended (unsupported amendments treated similarly); (f) where the EPO as ISA would not cite any documentary evidence (e.g., 'notorious knowledge' in CII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication and handling of partial top-up searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a top-up search is made for some claims or part of claims, there is no specific indication on the form of which claims are not covered by the top-up search or why only a partial top-up search was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information should be derivable from indications in Sections I and III of the WO/IPER; reasons for partial searches are not explicitly given on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of documents newly found in the top-up search
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents newly found in the top-up search are indicated and handled according to their publication date and potential relevance for novelty/inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published after filing date (E documents) and relevant for novelty -> mentioned in Section VI (detail per GL/PCT-EPO B-XI, 4.3). If published before priority date and relevant for novelty/inventive step -> mentioned in Section V with detailed reasoning. If published in priority period (P documents) and relevant -> mentioned in Section VI if priority assumed valid (comments optional unless other objections), but if priority invalid -> mentioned in Section V with detailed reasoning. Documents found during top-up and mentioned in WO-IPEA will also be mentioned in IPER unless rendered irrelevant by applicant's amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial action when top-up search reveals pertinent prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: If the top-up search reveals pertinent prior art, the first action in Chapter II is normally a WO-IPEA or a telephone consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a positive WO-ISA was drafted or objections in the negative WO-ISA have been overcome, different procedures apply (see GL/PCT-EPO C-IV, 5.4). Details of how documents are indicated are set out in GL/PCT-EPO sections and Rules (e.g., Rule 64.1, Rule 64.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes when top-up search results follow a positive WO-ISA or overcome objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a positive WO-ISA was drafted or objections overcome, the top-up search outcomes dictate whether a positive IPER or further WO-IPEA/telephone minutes are issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no relevant documents -> positive IPER. If pertinent prior art published before priority date -> WO-IPEA or telephone minutes. If only P/E documents which could become Art.54(3) prior art in later EP proceedings -> WO-IPEA with detailed novelty reasoning in Section VI. If other P/E documents relevant for novelty and priority assumed valid -> positive IPER with document mentioned in Section VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to pay additional examination fees under Chapter II after Chapter I lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invitation to pay additional fees was issued during Chapter I and the applicant paid some/all of the required additional fees and an objection to lack of unity was at least partly upheld during protest, under Chapter II the applicant will normally be invited (Form 405) to pay additional examination fees if the searched inventions are also to be examined under Chapter II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions for which no search fees were paid cannot be pursued and will not be objected to or commented on. A single WO-IPEA/IPER is drafted dealing with all inventions for which examination fees have been paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner considerations when claims are redrafted after WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: When the applicant files redrafted claims differing substantially from those for which lack of unity was raised, the examiner should consider whether the lack of unity objection still applies to the new set, whether amended claims relate to searched subject-matter, and whether the reasoning as to lack of unity must be amended because of new claims/arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally examiner under Chapter II agrees with search-stage objection; exceptionally examiner may send Form 405 even if not done at search stage (e.g., if search and WO-ISA by another office). If lack of unity at search stage resulted in partial search and a different conclusion is reached under Chapter II, there is no possibility to request additional search for unsearched matter—examination in Chapter II is restricted to what has been searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of additional search fees (Chapter II basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in reply to lack of unity at search stage, the applicant has not paid additional search fees, the WO-IPEA/IPER is based on the claims for which the search report and WO-ISA were drafted, taking amendments/arguments into account; Section IV is not filled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner proceeds only on searched claims; non-searched claims are not considered in IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of additional search fees without protest
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant paid additional search fees without protest and application still lacks unity, the lack of unity objection will normally be confirmed (where necessary adapted by amendments/arguments filed by applicant). Form 405 is sent requesting additional examination fees only for those inventions which have been searched and are still present in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section IV will be filled out and reasons for lack of unity given on separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of additional search fees under protest and Review Panel outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional search fees are paid under protest, the resulting Review Panel may decide the protest is fully, partly, or not justified, affecting whether Form 405 is sent and how WO-IPEA/IPER is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fully justified -> no Form 405 sent; WO-IPEA/IPER established for all searched inventions; reimburse all additional fees and protest fee. If partly justified -> Form 405 sent with adapted reasoning/number of inventions; reimburse corresponding additional fees but not protest fee. If not justified -> Form 405 sent/decision communicated with reasoning; examination on inventions for which fees paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must verify unity and searched status when applicant restricts claims or pays additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant restricts claims or pays additional fees in reply to Form 405, examiner must check that the restricted set is unitary and relates to searched subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restricted set is unitary and relates to searched subject-matter -> WO-IPEA/IPER established on restricted set and Section IV not filled. If not -> WO-IPEA/IPER established on main/first invention mentioned in Form 405 for which search fee paid; Section IV filled and claims relating to non-searched subject-matter indicated in Section III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of no request for payment of additional search fees at search stage
rubrics_metrics.description: If at search stage lack of unity was raised but no request to pay additional search fees was made, examination is carried out on the entire application; Section IV indicates the requirement of unity is not fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Form 405 is sent; WO-IPEA/IPER is established for all inventions (subject to other constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility requirements for a protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating the protest procedure formal admissibility under Rule 68.3(c) must be checked; the protest must satisfy specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: applicant must have paid the required fees under protest (Rule 68.3(e)) and paid the prescribed protest fee; payment under protest must be accompanied by a reasoned statement (filed with payment or at latest within time limit set in Form 405). The reasoned statement must comply with Rule 68.3(c): argue why the international application complies with unity or why the number of required additional examination fees is excessive (challenge number of additional fees, not the amount of a single fee). Formalities officers assess payment and filing; substantive analysis is by the Review Panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Panel scope and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The protest procedure consists of review within the IPEA first by the formalities officer and then by a Review Panel; the Review Panel's scope is limited to inventions for which additional fees have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's reasoning is not related to those inventions, protest will be found not or only partially justified. Review Panel decisions are communicated via Form 420 and will adapt the WO-IPEA/IPER and order reimbursements as appropriate; Form 420 is sent together with the WO-IPEA or IPER to ensure consistency. Names of Review Panel members are made public on Form 420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to start international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO as IPEA will not start the international preliminary examination before expiry of the time limit laid down in Rule 54bis, unless the applicant expressly requests an earlier start under Rule 69.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended applicants request an earlier start in the demand. Amendments/arguments under Article 34 filed after filing the demand but before expiry of this time limit will always be taken into account for international preliminary examination. The EPO does not apply Rules 69.1(b) and 69.1(b‑bis) (i.e., will not start the IPER concurrently with the international search).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the documents required for the preliminary examination were received in due time, the EPO will establish the IPER within 28 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has 31 months from the priority date to enter the European phase before the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time limits for replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of the time limit for replying to WO-ISA (first opinion of IPEA) and WO-IPEA are subject to strict conditions and limited extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule a one-month extension will be granted for replying to WO-ISA if requested before expiry and if extended time limit does not expire later than 25 months from earliest priority date; further extensions not allowed. Extension does not apply to the time limit for filing the demand. Request for extension to reply to a WO-IPEA will be granted only if sufficient time exists so that extended time limit does not expire later than 27 months from earliest priority date and request made before expiry. If the ISR was delayed so that 28-month IPER deadline cannot be met, request for extension should be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to telephone consultation (no personal interviews) and related effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Art.34(2) gives applicant right to communicate orally with the IPEA; telephone consultations should be granted but personal interviews are not granted (applicants requesting personal interview are offered telephone consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule applicant has right to one telephone consultation. After a telephone consultation applicant should generally be given a time limit (normally two months) to file amended claims/arguments. If applicant expresses intention not to file further observations and agrees to receive an IPER without further interaction, minutes are sent and directly followed up with a negative IPER (no time limit set). If consultation requested after issuance of further written opinion but before IPER establishment, request must be granted before a negative IPER is issued but applicant does not have right to file further amendments unless explicitly agreed. Matters for discussion should be clearly stated in advance; examiner records arrangement in file and sends a copy to applicant. If applicant wishes to discuss amended claims during consultation, a copy should be sent in advance. Result recorded and forwarded to applicant. If consultation replaces second written opinion and agreement on amendments reached, Form 428 includes warning that amendments cannot be made by IPEA and invitation to file amended sheets normally within one month but at least one month before IPER deadline. If no agreement reached, applicant informed arguments will be taken into account in IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and third-party access to IPER files
rubrics_metrics.description: Without applicant's authorisation, the IB and the EPO as IPEA may not allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination by third parties, except by elected Offices once the IPER has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once IPER established and transmitted to IB, IB sends copy and translation to each elected Office and thereafter furnishes copies to anyone who requests them. EPO as IPEA will provide access to any document in its file at request of any elected Office (except omitted information). Provided international publication has taken place, third parties may access file via elected Offices whose national law allows access to national application files; access may be allowed to the same extent as national law provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of third-party observations in Chapter II
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party observations relevant to Chapter II are taken into account in drafting WO-IPEA/IPER according to their timing and effect on the likely IPER outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a negative IPER is envisaged and a second written opinion not sent, a WO-IPEA is drafted taking into account applicant's comments and third-party observations, referring to new prior-art in Section V. If IPER would have been negative without third-party observations but a WO-IPEA already sent before receipt of observations, no further written opinion is sent before IPER establishment. If WO-IPEA already sent and IPER would have been positive without third-party observations, a new WO-IPEA is issued or the applicant called. In the above cases IPER is established taking into account third-party observations and applicant comments, referring to new documents in Section V. If positive IPER envisaged and third-party observations do not prejudice novelty/inventive step, newly cited relevant documents are dealt with in reasons in favour of patentability in Section V. Third-party observations not relevant or not sufficiently understandable need not be dealt with substantially; include a comment in Section V indicating they have been taken into account and found not relevant or could not be taken into account and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limitation of the IPER opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Art.35(2) specifies that the IPER shall not contain any statement on whether the claimed invention is or seems to be patentable or unpatentable according to any national law; the purpose is to give an opinion only and not to grant/refuse the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should not give the impression that any part of the application may or may not be allowable; it will only state whether or not the claims meet certain criteria. The IPER is drafted like the WO-ISA: a positive or negative opinion is given for all claims, taking into account arguments/amendments submitted by the applicant. The same criteria apply as to the WO-ISA with respect to examination issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPER establishment limited to searched claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPER will only be established for claims which have been searched (as indicated in the WO-ISA); amended claims directed to subject-matter not searched will not be considered and an indication will be made in Section III of the IPER with reasons given on the separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amended claims introducing unsearched matter are communicated as an inability to give an opinion for that subject-matter in the IPER (Rule 66.1(e), GL/ISPE 19.25).
